title: agent-platform definition inputs
description: The input set of the agent-platform capability: the installation's record and one choice. Everything the fileset carries derives from the record (installation.*: the registry and the installation's config.yaml.patch, read, never typed), from the fleet policy (policy.yaml: which components an owning organisation's installations run, the installations with a Slack app — where the chat gateway runs — and the gateway's shape, the hub's connector and Teleport cluster) and from the shared template; a person decides one thing, whether the installation serves models. Annotations: x-source says where a value comes from (registry: read from the installations registry or the repositories, never typed; generated: created once and read back from the checkout; person: the one choice). x-feature names the consistency feature of features.yaml. x-renders lists the key paths the input produces, prefixed by the file: configmap (agent-platform configmap-values.yaml.patch), dex-configmap (the dex-app patch), extras (extras/agent-platform/ and the MCP servers' extras), backstage:* (the portal's agent-platform Component), teleport (teleport-fleet). List indices are written [*], per-installation map keys <name>.

installation.description: The facts on record. Read from the installations registry, the installation's config.yaml.patch, the cluster App's manifest and the portals' app-configs; never typed and never in the form.

name.description: The installation's codename. Where the policy's klausGateway.installations names it, a Slack app exists for the installation and the chat gateway runs, its credentials supplied at commit; elsewhere no gateway renders.

baseDomain.description: The installation's base domain; every hostname of the platform (muster, agentgateway, dex, kagent, avatars) derives from it.

customer.description: The owning organisation as the configs repository names it; selects the policy's component list and the hub connector's name.

provider.description: The infrastructure provider; selects the cluster-manager's workload-cluster API pattern.

private.description: Reached through Teleport: a portal on record reaches the installation's Kubernetes API through the tunnel on the portal's host (kubernetes-<name>.agent-platform.svc.cluster.local) because the installation's ingress sits on private addresses. Its MCP servers then reach Dex on private addresses, muster accepts private client metadata and redirect URIs, and a hub brokers for it through the tunnel.

chartLine.description: The meta chart line the installation runs (agentPlatform.kagentApiV2 in config.yaml.patch selects 4): the 4 line pins the chart range, derives the managers' OAuth from the template's identity block and carries the serving slice.

musterClientId.description: The platform's Dex client id: services.muster.clientId of the installation's config.yaml.patch, else the shared default's. The template renders it; the definition uses it for the managers' OAuth on the 3 line and the live probes.

podCertificateRequest.description: Whether the cluster serves certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1 PodCertificateRequest, which kagent's Agent Substrate needs on the 4 chart line: true when the cluster App's values on record (management-clusters/<name>/cluster-app-manifests.yaml) enable the feature gates PodCertificateRequest, ClusterTrustBundle and ClusterTrustBundleProjection under cluster.internal.advancedConfiguration for the API server, the controller manager and the kubelet, or when the cluster App's chart enables them by default (giantswarm/cluster 8.3.0 and later: cluster-aws 10.3.0, cluster-azure 9.3.0, cluster-cloud-director 7.3.0). Renders nothing: a 4-line record with kagent and false is refused at plan time naming the gates and the path; true renders the live probe that discovers the API and reads rolling until it is served.

portals.description: The developer portals that sign people in on this installation: every portal whose gs.installations lists it, from the hub's app-config and the app-config of each customer-portal installation of the owning organisation. Each signs in through the definition's one Dex client (backstage, one redirect URI per portal); the platform's portal section is written into the organisation's own portal.

installation.description: The installation whose management-clusters tree hosts the portal.

customer.description: The host's owning organisation; the platform's portal section is written into the organisation's own portal only.

federation.description: The installation's place in the fleet's token exchange, from the portals' app-configs: the hubs whose broker exchanges tokens into it, and the targets its own muster brokers for.

hubs.description: Installations whose muster is the cluster-token broker of a portal that lists this one: each renders a token-exchange client in this installation's Dex.

targets.description: Installations this one brokers for: the portal whose cluster-token broker is this installation's muster lists them. Each target's own three MCP servers (kubernetes, prometheus, capi) join muster's list with exchange auth; a private target is reached through the tunnel. An installation with targets is a hub: its broker also carries the `github` grant target (grantIssuer https://github.com/login/oauth, in its broker client's audiences), which releases the person's own GitHub grant to the hub's Dev Portal — no GitHub App in the portal.

private.description: The target's record: reached through Teleport, so this hub tunnels to it — a RemoteApp per tunnelled app on this hub and the app's tunnel entry among this hub's entries of teleport-fleet's tunnelport values; the tunnel's bots join by this hub's published service-account issuer (irsa.<base domain> on capa; another provider refuses a private target).

brokerClientId.description: Dex client id of the hub's token-exchange broker client; registered once, read back from the hub's patch afterwards. Required on a hub.

modelServing.description: The one choice: whether the installation serves models.

enabled.description: Serve models on this installation: the llm-d control plane, the well-known LLMInferenceServiceConfigs, the model serving switch and the models Gateway (the meta chart's serving slice, 4.44.0 and later). The 4 chart line only; the GPU pool is the cluster-manager's.
